node.title: Re^3: LibXML setNodeName error (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I remember doing battle with [mod://XML::LibXML] in a similar situation a few years ago. IIRC, what I found back then is that the problem is namespaces - note how the document originally has only one namespace (http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform) with only one namespace prefix (xsl). What you're asking to do is move the node into a completely different namespace, specifically in this case the default one. I remember not being able to find the appropriate combinations of API calls to achieve this so that the resulting XML looked clean, and playing around by adding $element->setNamespace(...); to [choroba]'s code seems to confirm this, the best I can do so far is . It seemed that once a node has been created in a namespace, it's stuck there you can't get it back into the default namespace cleanly. Back then I ended up writing a routine to create a new node in the new namespace. Now since this was a while ago, it's possible I missed the appropriate API function, but even now going through the [mod://XML::LibXML] docs and Googling a bit I still don't see an obvious way.

Caveat: The below will completely ignore any other attributes in the element being replaced, so for example if you've got or use-attribute-sets, that will be ignored and lost!

Here's what my workaround would look like (based in part on [choroba]'s code):

use warnings; use strict; use XML::LibXML; my $xml = <<'END_XML'; END_XML my $doc = XML::LibXML->load_xml(string => $xml) or die; my $xpc = XML::LibXML::XPathContext->new($doc); for my $el ($xpc->findnodes('//xsl:element')) { my $newel = $doc->createElement($el->getAttribute('name')); $newel->appendChild($_) for $el->childNodes; $el->replaceNode($newel); } print $doc; __END__

Update: Made description more accurate.
